h.strategy: Use retrieved findings to classify settings as strong, weak, neutral or harmful, and to identify which settings can disconnect other parts from the outcome. Propose hypotheses only of two kinds. Self-conditioning: the edit's effect depends on the value it replaces, being more negative when that value is strong and more positive when it is empty or harmful. Disconnection: when the edited part cannot influence the outcome, its effect shrinks toward zero, so the direction is lower if the edit usually helps and higher if it usually hurts. Directions refer to the signed effect. For each hypothesis, state the edit's usual sign and a one-sentence mechanism. Cover varied edit fields and values. The critic should replace any hypothesis with an uncertain usual sign, competing effects or reliance on partial redundancy.

hyps.why: Usual sign positive; replacing none restores the entire 2->3 route, a bigger gain than upgrading an op that already carries signal.
Usual sign positive; replacing an already strong conv leaves little room to gain compared with replacing weaker ops.
Usual sign negative; deleting a conv3x3 on the 2->3 route loses far more capacity than deleting a skip or pool.
Setting conv1x1 over conv3x3 is a downgrade of the strongest op, so the effect is more negative than when replacing none, skip or pool.
Usual sign negative; swapping the input-edge feature extractor for identity loses the most capacity when the replaced op is conv3x3.
Usual sign positive; with 0->1 removed node 1 has no input, so edge 2 cannot influence the output and the gain shrinks to zero.
Usual sign positive; edge 4 starts at the signal-less node 1, so its upgrade carries nothing to the output.
Usual sign positive; node 2 only exits via edge 5, so with edge 5 removed the upgrade cannot reach node 3.
Usual sign positive; edge 1 feeds only node 2, which is cut off from the output when edge 5 is none, so the gain vanishes.
Usual sign negative; removing edge 1 normally costs a route, but when node 2 is already cut off the removal is irrelevant, so the loss shrinks toward zero.
